biggestGap: Now that the confetti is largely gone and the collar is a lit shell, the tell is the flesh itself: the cut face is a smooth, flat, low-saturation brick-red field whose ONLY internal detail is a 1-2 px dither, where plate-01's face is a dense mesh of resolved pale radial fibre bundles over crimson with juice pooled in the grooves - our speck median area is 2 px with 36.0% single-pixel against the plate's 6 px and 16.4%, and our flesh G/R is 0.4448 against 0.3392.
evidence: ⚠ PROBE_VERSION BUMPED 4 -> 5. I ADDED ONE PROBE, `foam`, AND SAY SO LOUDLY. No existing probe's code changed by one character; `suite shots/r5` under v5 reproduces all 14 pre-existing rows byte-identically (verified by reconstructing a v4 file from the v5 source, running both, and diffing the JSON: MISMATCHED ROWS = NONE; clip:05 5.227 mask 9490, ring:05 3.354 mask 3763, particles:15 n=67 medArea 4.0 sat 0.7982, particles:16 n=48 medArea 15.5 sat 0.8103). The bump is bookkeeping, not an invalidation. WHY IT HAD TO EXIST: the brief asks three questions about the named defect - are the pips FEWER, MORE VARIED, UNCLIPPED - and `clip` answers only the third and only partly, because it reports one scalar (pct_R_ge_255) with no count and no size distribution, AND because its region is the second-moment ellipse of the largest luma component of the WHOLE FRAME, which on 05-cut+500ms is both melon halves plus rind plus the juice bridging them (30-34% of it is green rind). It is not the cut face. That is exactly why the r5 critic, the r5 builder and the r6 builder each hand-rolled a third ruler for this property and got 13.6%, 4.89% and 1.50%. `foam` fixes the region (explicit window, printed; inside it largest_component(luma>8); its second-moment ellipse at scale 0.80, taken WHOLE and NOT intersected with the luma mask so dark seeds stay in the denominator) and reports TWO populations: `whitish_*` (G>0.75R, the r5 verdict's own definition, so the handed-forward number stays comparable) and `speck_*` (luma exceeds its own local 7x7 median luma by 18 - pure morphology, hue-blind, the number to trust). ── (1) THE FROZEN `clip` ROW, QUOTED AS ASKED. clip 05-cut+500ms: r5 5.227% R>=255 mask 9490 -> r6 5.162% mask 6858; plate-01 0.400% mask 362926. FLAT. But the mask moved 28% (the ellipse went a/b 61.7/55.9 -> 60.6/38.9) because stage.js defocused the streak and the halves repose, so this row is a weaker comparison than its two decimal places suggest - which is precisely why the cut-face question needed its own region. ── (2) `foam 05-cut+500ms` LOWER MELON HALF, win=208:300:288:392, region 5522 -> 5487 px (STABLE, 0.6%), plate-01 win=320:565:545:805 region 42154 px. CLIPPING: 468 -> 372 px, 8.475% -> 6.780% of the face (plate 0.728%). Down 20%, still 9.3x the plate, and 85.5% of every clipped pixel is still a pip (r5 86.5%) - so the clipping on this face is STILL essentially all foam, unchanged in character. FEWER: whitish_n 104 -> 53, a genuine halving; on the UPPER half (win 160:215:290:390 / 168:220:295:390) whitish_n 54 -> 25 and speck_n 108 -> 59. MORE VARIED: whitish_pct_single_px 43.3 -> 35.8 (plate 19.2), whitish_area_p95_over_median 6.35 -> 22.9 - a real heavy tail where there was none. ── (3) BUT THE COLOUR-BLIND CONTROL SAYS THE POPULATION BARELY MOVED, AND ITS SHAPE GOT WORSE. speck_n 143 -> 136 (-5%), speck_cov_pct 23.99 -> 20.87 (plate 17.50), speck_median_area 3 -> 2 (plate 6), speck_pct_single_px 28.7 -> 36.0 (plate 16.4). The whitish count halved and the hue-blind count did not, and I can show why: G>0.75R is a RATIO and fires on any near-neutral DARK pixel, so a face that got darker sheds partially-covered pips from the whitish set without them leaving the screen. Proof from my own probe on the upper half: whitish_cov_pct 7.13 -> 18.32 while whitish_mean_rgb FELL (149,131,98) -> (130,120,72) and speck_n halved. I have written that contamination into probes.py so no one quotes whitish_cov_pct as a foam number again. Net honest answer to the brief: fewer YES (about half), more varied YES on size, unclipped ONLY 20% and still 9.3x plate, and the residual bright texture is now 1-2 px dither that is no longer foam - it is the fibre/seed-halo noise underneath it, at the same sub-resolved scale. ── (4) THE COLLAR IS THE ROUND'S CLEAREST WIN AND IT IS STRUCTURAL. I did not steer by `ring` (3.354 -> 3.619, plate 5.514) because the r6 builder is right that its band is not the collar - I rendered the whitish connected components instead. r5's collar is ONE closed component of 1407 px, perfectly concentric and constant width all the way round. r6's is 1332 + 411 px as SEPARATE arcs with visibly varying width - thick on the lower-left, thin on the right, absent mid-right. It is a lit shell now, not a drawn ring, and it is the difference between the two crops at a glance. ── (5) THE ROUND-5 RED-CHANNEL WIN HELD; I CHECKED BEFORE ACCUSING. Lower face flesh (whitish removed) (141.4,71.9,51.1) -> (125.7,55.9,37.8), plate (189.2,64.2,47.8): R down 11%. But the upper face is FLAT, (102.3,32.9,11.6) -> (100.4,35.2,12.1), and the whole-melon skin frame 01 got BRIGHTER (subject mean luma 65.93 -> 70.56), so there is no global dim; the lower half's ellipse went a/b 1.058 -> 1.195, i.e. it is posed more edge-on this round. I record the red channel as HELD, not regressed. And flesh G/R moved 0.5083 -> 0.4448 against plate 0.3392 - the first movement toward the plate in four rounds, closing 37% of the gap, after r3 0.528 -> r4 0.506 -> r5 0.577 went the other way three times. Face contrast also improved: pct_lum_le_25 5.02 -> 5.30 (plate 4.24), med_over_p2 5.74 -> 6.42 (plate 7.87); seeds are now dark enough that parts of them fall below the luma-8 subject floor. ── (6) ⚠ THE SUITE'S clip:08-citrus-caps ROW IS MEASURING THE BLADE STREAK IN r6 AND MUST NOT BE QUOTED. r5 1.711% mask 2104 (ellipse a=29.4 b=22.8) -> r6 1.171% mask 4525 with ellipse a=142.7 b=10.65 - a horizontal sliver spanning the frame. The largest luma component of r6's 08 frame is the streak, not the fruit. The number is not a fruit statistic and the apparent improvement is an artefact. ── (7) WHAT DID NOT MOVE AT ALL, TWO ROUNDS RUNNING. The orange peel is still a REGULAR SQUARE LATTICE of hard dark dots, plainly visible at 1.5x on 08-citrus-caps - named in the r4 and r5 verdicts, untouched. The watermelon skin stripes are a repeating hard-edged sawtooth band with an identical triangular period in every stripe and a blue cast on the shadow side, against plate-01's soft irregular mottling. Credit where due: the orange CUT face gained real radial segment spokes and is no longer the featureless golden-white blob the r5 verdict named. ── (8) BLIND. r6 05 cut face against plate-01's melon face at matched apparent size: I pick the render, and unlike round 5 I no longer pick it on the confetti or on the ring. I pick it on the flesh interior. Plate-01's face is a dense mesh of pale radial fibre bundles, 4-8 px at that size, with crimson ground between them and juice standing in the grooves; ours is a smooth brown-red field with black seed slabs laid on top and a 1-2 px sparkle over it. The r6 face genuinely reads as watermelon flesh where r5's read as a red disc with glitter - that is the whole of the +6 - but it reads as CG watermelon flesh instantly.
fix: In /home/claude/juice/src/fruit/species.js, apply the round-6 rule - 'nothing below the pixel goes into the normal' - to the FLESH BODY, not just to the foam. `blobFade` and `micro` were aimed at wetField's two bead octaves and they worked; the melon flesh's own detail (the `ringN(ang, ...)` fibre term and the `fbm2` octaves in the watermelon `relief`/`albedo`) was never routed through the same guard, which is why the surviving 1-2 px sparkle is no longer foam and why speck_median_area is 2 px against plate-01's 6 px with 36.0% single-pixel against 16.4%. Two changes, one file: (a) route every flesh detail octave through `blobFade` at its own feature radius and dump the rejected variance into `roughnessNode` alongside `micro`, exactly as wetField already does - anything under ~3 px must become sheen, not speckle; (b) replace the rejected fine noise with ONE resolved anisotropic radial fibre field: pale bundles running centre-outward at a 14-20 px pitch at review size (so 4-8 px wide, above the derivative footprint), lifting albedo and dropping saturation ON the bundle while the ground between bundles is pulled toward the plate's hue, which is the same lever that closes flesh_GR 0.4448 -> 0.3392. Verify with the FROZEN probe, never a hand mask: `python3 tools/probes.py foam shots/r7/05-cut+500ms.png` (default win=208:300:288:392, region ~5500 px - quote mask_px) must satisfy ALL FIVE in one frame: speck_median_area >= 4 (plate 6), speck_pct_single_px <= 22 (plate 16.4), speck_cov_pct 17-21 (plate 17.5), flesh_GR 0.34 +/- 0.03 (plate 0.3392), pct_R_ge_255 <= 2.0 (plate 0.728, we are at 6.780). Do NOT quote whitish_cov_pct - the probe's own docstring now records that it is contaminated by dark neutrals. Do not touch the collar; it is fixed.
notes: 55 -> 61, the largest single-round gain this piece has had, and the first time it crosses out of 'clearly a game render'. Both defects handed forward moved for real. The collar is structurally fixed - r5's whitish map is one closed 1407 px constant-width ring, r6's is 1332+411 px broken arcs of varying width - and that is a first-glance difference. The foam halved in count (whitish_n 104 -> 53 lower face, 54 -> 25 upper) and vanished outright from the upper half by eye, face clipping fell 8.475% -> 6.780%, G/R moved toward the plate for the first time in four rounds, and the round-5 red-channel win held (upper face flat 102.3 -> 100.4; the lower face's -11% is a pose change, and the untouched-material control frame 01 got BRIGHTER, so there is no global dim). Two things keep it at 61 rather than higher. First, the hue-blind speck population barely moved (n 143 -> 136, coverage 24.0 -> 20.9) and its shape went the wrong way (single-pixel 28.7% -> 36.0% against the plate's 16.4%), so the sub-resolved sparkle is not gone, it has changed owner from the foam to the flesh's own fibre noise. Second, two long-standing defects were not touched for a second round: the orange peel's regular square dot lattice and the watermelon skin's repeating sawtooth stripe. PROCESS. I bumped PROBE_VERSION 4 -> 5 to add `foam` and verified all 14 pre-existing r5 rows reproduce byte-identically. Two instrument findings worth carrying forward regardless of who reads this: (i) the suite's clip:08-citrus-caps row is fitting its ellipse to the BLADE STREAK in r6 (a=142.7 b=10.65, mask 2104 -> 4525) and its number is not a fruit statistic; (ii) my own new whitish_cov_pct is contaminated by dark neutral pixels and I have written that warning into probes.py rather than let the next round quote it. The r6 builder also deserves credit for a negative result honestly reported: they wrote a `collar` probe, found it inverted against human judgement on plate-01, and deleted it rather than ship a fourth misnamed ruler.
